newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour leader admits error in school row.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour leader admits error in school row.

text.p: British opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair disclosed on Monday that he had made a major misjudgment in failing to spot the trouble that would be sparked by a colleague's choice of school for her younger son.

In an interview with Reader's Digest, he said failing to predict the furore that ensued from the decision of his shadow cabinet colleague Harriet Harman to send her son to a grammar (selective) school was his biggest error since taking over as Labour leader in 1994.
Harman chose earlier this year to send the younger of her two sons to a grammar school, rather than follow the party line and send him to a comprehensive (non-selective) school.
Blair said: "I was too slow to recognize what would happen after Harriet Harman's decision on the school.
"I regarded it as a straightforward private matter, and I felt that was very important.
"I thought the reaction was way over the top, but I should have gone public more quickly and explained it."
The decision by Harman, Labour's social security spokeswoman, triggered serious in-fighting within the Labour Party and charges of hypocrisy against Harman and Blair himself.
Blair has admitted in the past that the Harman episode was his lowest moment as leader, but this is the first time he has conceded publicly that the gaffe was his.
